locator.text: Display 35.5, p. 35, in the statement of Lemma 4.8

evidence: paper: X_R < X_{\mathrm{good}} < \inf \mathcal{I}_1, \qquad \sup \mathcal{I}_4 < X_{\mathrm{v}} < X_{\mathrm{tail}} < X_{\mathrm{b}} = e^{3} X_{\mathrm{tail}},

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. The Lean works in the logarithmic clock y = log(X/X_R) (OutgoingDilation.clock / radius XR y = XR·exp y) and states the chain link by link rather than as one display; `radius_strictMono` turns each clock inequality into the radius inequality, so the two orderings are the same statement. Dictionary used: X_R ↔ y = 0; X_good ↔ radius XR holdStart (the left edge of `OutgoingCone.trueWindow`, the rectangle on which the admissible/TrueAt condition is asserted, OutgoingCone.lean:389); inf I_1 / sup I_4 ↔ ReservedPatches.left F XR .modulation and .right F XR .mean, whose clocks are pulseStart − 25 and pulseStart − 3 (the file's own docstring names the four manuscript intervals (−25,−20), (−20,−15), (−14,−9), (−8,−3), so I_2 is the heat slot as the paper says); X_v ↔ OutgoingDilation.pulseEndRadius = radius XR endpoint; X_tail ↔ radius XR (tailStart) (consistent with cleanEnd = tailStart + 1/2 ↔ the paper's e^{1/2}X_tail); X_b ↔ OutgoingDilation.tailRadius = radius XR (tailStart + 3), so the paper's equality X_b = e^3 X_tail is definitional in Lean. The paper's side condition that the interval endpoints divided by X_R are fixed independently of X_R and η also holds definitionally, since left/right = XR·exp(clock) with the clock depending only on the profile parameters. No single Lean declaration states the whole chain.
